title: Claude 20x Renamed to Ultra, Removes 5-Hour Usage Cap
summary: Anthropic rebrands Claude 20x as Claude Ultra and eliminates the controversial 5-hour usage limit. New tier offers unlimited flagship model access.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Anthropic rebrands Claude 20x subscription tier to Claude Ultra, removing the restrictive 5-hour usage cap.
- Ultra plan now offers unlimited access to flagship Claude models without time-based restrictions on heavy workloads.
- Change addresses user complaints about artificial usage limits disrupting professional workflows and long research sessions.


Anthropic has officially rebranded its Claude 20x subscription tier as Claude Ultra and eliminated the controversial 5-hour usage cap that previously restricted access to flagship models. The change, confirmed on October 30, 2026, marks a significant shift in how the AI lab structures premium access to its most capable language models.


## What Changed in the Ultra Rebrand


The former Claude 20x tier has been renamed Claude Ultra, but the changes go beyond cosmetic branding. Most notably, Anthropic removed the 5-hour time limit that previously capped how long subscribers could use flagship Claude models in intensive sessions. This limit had been a point of friction for professional users running extended research tasks, code generation workflows, and multi-hour analysis projects.


Under the previous 20x structure, users hitting the 5-hour threshold would be automatically downgraded to lighter models or face session interruptions. The new Ultra tier eliminates this constraint entirely, offering uninterrupted access to top-tier Claude models regardless of session duration or computational intensity.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on October 30, 2026, the Claude Ultra plan is now available to all existing 20x subscribers and new customers through Anthropic's standard subscription portal. Existing 20x users were automatically transitioned to Ultra branding with the updated usage terms taking effect immediately.


## Pricing and Competitive Context


While Anthropic has not disclosed whether the rebrand includes pricing adjustments, industry observers note the move aligns Claude's premium tier more closely with competitors offering unlimited flagship model access. OpenAI's[GPT-6 Astra](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-opus-5-5-vs-gpt-6-astra) and[GPT-6 Sol](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-opus-5-5-vs-gpt-6-sol) plans, as well as Google's Gemini Advanced tier, already provide uncapped usage for their most capable models.


The removal of time-based throttling suggests Anthropic is prioritizing user experience and professional workflows over hard computational caps. For enterprises and power users, this means uninterrupted access for tasks like:


- Multi-hour code refactoring and debugging sessions
- Extended document analysis and synthesis workflows
- Long-form content generation requiring iterative refinement
- Complex research tasks spanning multiple hours of continuous interaction


## User Response and Industry Impact


The 5-hour limit had drawn criticism from developers and researchers who found artificial time caps disruptive to deep work. By eliminating this constraint, Anthropic signals confidence in its infrastructure's ability to handle sustained premium workloads without arbitrary throttling.


The rebrand also simplifies Anthropic's tier naming. Claude Ultra is more intuitive than the numeric 20x designation, making it easier for new users to understand the premium positioning without decoding multiplier semantics.


## What This Means


Anthropic's move to rebrand Claude 20x as Ultra and remove usage caps reflects growing competitive pressure in the premium AI subscription market. As flagship models become more capable and compute-intensive, providers are shifting from time-based throttling to more flexible access models. For professionals relying on Claude for mission-critical work, the change removes a key friction point and positions Ultra as a true unlimited-access tier. Users seeking maximum Claude performance can now subscribe without worrying about mid-session interruptions or arbitrary time constraints.
